dct_description_sm:
The two Mehri tracking texts provided in Watson (2012) are 20110226_MehriRabkut_M004_FirstCar and 20110227_MehriRabkut_M083_WadiStory. Here the transcriptions and translations have been revised in the Praat textgrids provided. The text 20141104_MehriDhahbun_M043_cameltracking is accompanied by an ELAN file with transcription and translation. The Shehret audio files have not yet been transcribed or translated.

Selim identifies tracks is the latest children's story in Mehri, translated into English. It teaches children the Mehri names of wild and domestic animals and encourages them to identify particular tracks.

This is a set of Mehri and Shehret audio texts produced in Dhofar, Oman that relate to the knowledge and practice of tracking in southern Arabia. Traditionally conducted by men, who learn to track from a young age, the texts provide stories and descriptions of tracking individual camels, people or car tracks.

The set also includes the powerpoint version of Selim identifies tracks, a children's book in Mehri and translated into English by Abdullah al-Mahri, Janet Watson, Hussein al-Mahri and Sulaiman al-Mahri, with illustrations by Matthew Logue.
